Dr Vincent Raymond
Cardiologist
422 Wickham Tce
Brisbane
08-08-2009
Dear Dr Raymond,
RE: Mrs Dulcie Wood DOB: 15-07-1943
I am writing to refer Mrs Wood, a 66-year-old widow, who presented with features suggestive of atrial fibrillation. I scheduled appointment with your receptionist at 8 am on 14-08-2009.
On 03-07-2009, Mrs Wood firstly presented with uncomfortable sensation in her chest several times in the preceding weeks. On examination, there was a mild elevation of her blood pressure (145/70), and her heart rate was 80 per minute and regular. I advised her to record the frequency of fibrillation bouts and I prescribed Noten. 2 weeks later, she returned complaining of waking up at night despite improvement of fibrillation sensation. Accordingly, Noten dose was increased.
On today's review, Mrs Wood reported initial improvement of her condition. However, there was an increase in the fluttery sensation in the last 3 days. She was anxious and upset as she has a strong family history of acute myocardial infarction. She wanted to be referred to you as you treated her sister before. Her blood pressure was 180/70 mmHg. 
In view of the above, I would appreciate it if you could assess Mrs Wood and provide advice regarding the management of her condition.
Should you require any further information, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,
Doctor
